feature.title: Rhythm tracker replan after D11
feature.request: in the last session, we made progress on resolving regressions with summer2000 and low-bpm-rnb, but the orchestrator came back and said we needed to replan some work. Please look at everything it did and replan these features (there are still open PRs that im working on merging too)

problem.statement: After the D11 run, summer2000 is still 153 ms off the beat (target 40). D11's S1 trace showed that none of the evidence BeatTracker has (summed onset, per-band flux, a looser streak gate) points at the taps. Only the worklet's BandOnsets kick events do (a median 31 ms before the taps), and they never reach the analyzer today, because rhythmTracker.ts onMessage forwards only frames. Every move that lands the grid on the taps slides off within 2 s: through the 12-14.8 s fill the per-beat correction follows the envelope's strongest onset, and once the grid is more than BEAT_WINDOW_FRACTION from the kicks it never sees them again. The tracker needs a new input (kick events) and a way to hold a phase hypothesis against an envelope that disagrees and to ride out fills. Beat presence (beatless) and bar-level beat (6-8-time, half-time-shuffle) failed in D11 for lack of the same kind of evidence. low-bpm-rnb (S4b) and the dotted 3/2 change (S7) were fixed in D11 PRs that are still merging.
users: Trevor, the developer, who judges tracker changes on the scorecard
Listeners watching any visualizer, whose visuals follow tracker.state beat phase
evidence: d11 hub-scorecard.md 'Tracker plan D11, S1': the phase check's best window sits on the grid at bin 1, and the taps at bins 6-10. Band-0 flux also peaks at bin 1, while kick events peak 0.25-0.375 beat into the grid, near the taps

d11 hub-scorecard.md S1 prototype table: kick events in the phase bins, a half-beat flip, a kick-preferring correction and a longer gate give 149.5 ms at best. Moves onto the taps slide off within 2 s
rhythmTracker.ts:228-244 forwards only time0, frames and count to analyzer.pushBatch. FeatureBatch (types.ts:77-100) already carries onsetBand, onsetTime and onsetStrength
audioHub.ts:274-341 is today's only onset consumer and releases events at render time
d11 S6 and S8 records: no autocorrelation-based presence signal and no tie-multiple bar evidence separated beatless or 6-8-time without breaking blocking cells

goals: Bring summer2000 beat.errorMedianMs to 40 ms or less, in at most two bounded attempts (required)
Give the analyzer and BeatTracker the worklet's kick events as an input, in time order, with no per-frame allocation
Keep every passing blocking cell, the S4b low-bpm-rnb result (at most 40 ms) and the S7 dotted change, with no added sweep:gate false opens
Stretch: reuse the kick-event evidence for beat presence (beatless) and bar-level beat (6-8-time, half-time-shuffle), each shipped or reverted on its own
Re-record the live cells (AC7 dance-clip consistency, gate seconds) once the D11 PRs and this plan's required slice merge
non_goals: Re-doing D11 work that shipped (S4b halving re-search, S7 dotted rule) or retrying the measured misses (kick-weighted phase bins, a looser streak gate, the autocorrelation presence floor, tie multiples alone)
Changing scorecard targets (v9) or the tapped .beats.json truth
Hub, visualizer, bassGate or dance-clip code changes. Gate seconds are reported under D9, not tuned
A finer low-end spectrum for bassline-kick-120 onsets (accepted in D11)
Changing the worklet's onset detector or moving the tracker into the worklet; three.js upgrades

Every tracker change is judged on the full npm run scorecard, scorecard:check, sweep:gate and bench:tracker

decisions.question: Which D11 PRs does the plan assume?
decisions.answer: All of them: S1 trace tools, S2 pins, S4b, S5 and S7 merge as they are. The plan starts on post-merge main and rebases if one changes

decisions.question: What does the replan cover?
decisions.answer: Required: summer2000 through a kick-event phase input. Stretch: beat presence and bar-level beat, using the same evidence
decisions.rationale: summer2000 is the only required cell still failing

decisions.question: Budget?
decisions.answer: Total JS up to +3 kB (341.5 kB), raised in the PR that needs it; tracker CPU at most 1.25x, measured interleaved
decisions.rationale: Same as D11; room for a few phase hypotheses

decisions.question: What if summer2000 misses 40 ms?
decisions.answer: Two bounded attempts, each with a pre-registered grid. If both miss, record them and accept the cell at its measured value

decisions.question: Where do kick events come from?
decisions.answer: The existing worklet BandOnsets in FeatureBatch (onsetBand, onsetTime, onsetStrength), forwarded by rhythmTracker.onMessage. The worklet and the message version stay unchanged
decisions.rationale: types.ts:77-100 already carries them; rhythmTracker.ts:228-244 drops them

decisions.question: Is gate.secondsAfterLock required?
decisions.answer: No. It is reported, and passing tracks must not get worse (D9 of D11 carries over)
decisions.rationale: Carried from the D11 plan; bassGate is a non-goal

decisions.question: Does a phase move bump gridEpoch?
decisions.answer: No. A phase move counts in phaseShiftCount; only a numbering break bumps the epoch
decisions.rationale: beatTracker.ts epoch specs; an epoch change shrinks the meter's evidence (rhythmAnalyzer.ts)

decisions.question: Is the framing confirmed?
decisions.answer: Yes, as shown at the full-lane checkpoint

decisions.question: Is there a baseline slice first?
decisions.answer: Yes. S0 waits for the D11 PRs, then re-runs scorecard and the live cells on post-merge main and rewrites the baseline as the before values, in one docs-only PR
decisions.rationale: Every later slice needs a stable before

options.summary: Forward band-0 kick events through rhythmTracker and analyzer into a small fixed ring in BeatTracker, and let a kick-phase vote (circular mean of kick offsets against the grid) gate and pull the existing per-beat correction, with no new tracker state machine.
approach: rhythmTracker.onMessage passes onsetBand, onsetTime, onsetStrength and an onset count to analyzer.pushBatch as optional fields. No worklet or message version change (D5).

rhythmAnalyzer.pushBatch walks frames and kick events with one merged index, so each kick (onsetBand 0) is delivered once, before the first frame whose time is at or after the event time. Events that lead the batch's frames wait in the ring.
BeatTracker.pushKick(time, strength) writes into a preallocated Float64Array ring of 16 recent kicks. No allocation.
On each beat boundary, BeatTracker computes the kick phase: strength-weighted circular mean of (kickTime - lastBeatTime) / period over kicks in the last 4 beats, plus a concentration value R.

If R is above a threshold and the mean offset exceeds a dead-band, the correction target is the kick phase and not the envelope's strongest onset. The move is bounded per beat, goes through the existing phase-move path (phaseShiftCount++, gridEpoch kept), and holds across fills because the kick ring outlives envelope disagreement.
With R below the threshold, or with no kicks, the existing code path runs unchanged. That gives the AC3 identity spec: no kicks, same output as main.

Pre-register two attempts. Attempt 1 uses a 4-beat window with the kick phase as target. Attempt 2 uses an 8-beat window plus a hold that blocks envelope moves while R stays high. Record both in hub-scorecard.md.

contracts: analyzer.pushBatch accepts optional onsetBand, onsetTime, onsetStrength and onsetCount
BeatTracker.pushKick(time: number, strength: number): void, called in time order before push()
No change to tracker.state or to the getters lastBeatTime, periodSeconds, beatCount, gridEpoch, phaseShiftCount, gridHitShare
pros: Small diff of about 100 lines, roughly 0.5 kB of JS
Falls back to existing behaviour when kicks are absent or weak, so passing cells are protected
Stretch slices can reuse the ring and R (R as a presence cue, kick-offset histogram for bars)
cons: Headroom is tight (0.4 kB under the limit); the JS limit may need a small raise
A phase vote is a heuristic. It may still lose to the dense fill at 12 to 14.8 s on summer2000
Tuning thresholds per attempt risks overfitting one track
risks: Kick events land about 31 ms before the taps, so the target needs a learned or constant lead compensation, and a wrong constant leaves a floor above 40 ms
Kicks may mislead on tracks where the worklet's kick band fires on bass lines (bassline-kick-120)
Merge ordering bugs when a batch's events lead its frames
uncovered_acs: AC8 (re-recording is a docs step after the required slice)

options.summary: Forward kick events through a time-ordered, allocation-free channel into BeatTracker, and let a decayed kick-phase histogram act as a hysteresis-guarded prior that vetoes envelope-driven phase moves and freezes corrections through fills.
approach: rhythmTracker.onMessage passes onsetBand/onsetTime/onsetStrength (kick band only) to analyzer.pushBatch; no worklet or message-version change (D5). The batch's kick arrays are copied into a fixed-size KickQueue ring (capacity above the worklet buffer size, overflow drops oldest and counts it) so transferred buffers are not retained.

Analyzer drains the queue per frame: an event is released to beat.pushKick(time, strength) once frame time minus the ~100 ms analysis delay passes event time, so each event is seen exactly once and in order, even when a batch's events lead its frames. Empty queue means zero calls, so output equals main (AC3 spec).

BeatTracker keeps a KickPhaseModel: a preallocated Float32Array of 8 bins per beat period, weighted by strength, exponentially decayed per beat, re-binned only on period change. It yields kickPhase, support (peak share) and margin over the current grid phase.

Phase moves gain a guard. An envelope-driven correction is applied only if the kick model does not contradict it (the target phase's kick support is at least the current phase's minus a margin). A kick-driven move fires only after margin holds for N consecutive beats (hysteresis), and it counts in phaseShiftCount without bumping gridEpoch (D7).

Fill hold: when envelope onset strength is high but kick support at the grid phase has been steady over the last K beats, freeze per-beat correction (the 12-14.8 s fill) and let the grid coast on the period. The hold releases after M beats with no kick support at all, so lost tempo still recovers.

Two pre-registered attempts (D4). A: veto plus hysteresis only. B: add the fill hold and a half-beat candidate seeded from the kick histogram. Record each grid, result and trace:beats output in hub-scorecard.md. Stretch beat-presence and bar-level slices read the same kick support and margin, and ship or revert separately.

Tests: spec for kick ordering and exactly-once delivery with leading events; the no-kick identity spec; a synthetic with a disagreeing envelope and a fill that holds the kick phase; the S2, S4b and S7 specs unchanged.

contracts: analyzer.pushBatch(batch) reads the existing onsetBand, onsetTime and onsetStrength fields (no type change)
BeatTracker.pushKick(time: number, strength: number): void, called in non-decreasing time order, before the frame whose time is at or after the event
BeatTracker read-only getters kickSupport and kickMargin for the stretch slices; existing getters keep their meaning
pros: Directly targets both failure modes in the S1 trace: sliding off the taps and fills dragging the grid
Hysteresis and the release path bound the damage when kick evidence is wrong, which keeps the 0 kick-track case identical to main
The same support and margin signals serve the stretch slices
Clean boundary: the queue and the model are unit-testable apart from BeatTracker
cons: Largest change of the options: two new modules plus tunables, with a 0.4 kB size headroom problem (likely needs part of the +3 kB raise)
More parameters to tune against a single track, so overfit risk
risks: Kicks sit 31 ms before the taps, so the guard may hold a grid near the kicks and still miss 40 ms; an offset prior may be needed
Veto can lock a wrong phase on tracks where kicks are off-beat (syncopation); the release rule and the scorecard cover that
Kick events over fixed-size worklet buffers can drop; the overflow counter exposes this
Tuning on 1 track can break low-bpm-rnb or the S7 dotted rule

options.summary: Stop trying to make the BeatTracker's own grid hold against the envelope; leave it untouched and add a downstream KickPhase estimator that learns a slow, circular median offset between kick events and the grid, applied only at the analyzer output.
approach: Break the assumption that the correction loop must be the place the kick evidence acts: every D11 move onto the taps slid off because the loop re-learned from the envelope. Keep BeatTracker's grid, period, epoch and shift logic as they are.

rhythmTracker.onMessage forwards onsetBand/onsetTime/onsetStrength; analyzer.pushBatch merges kick events (band 0) with frames in time order using a read cursor over the batch arrays, so there is no allocation.

KickPhase keeps a fixed-size ring of the last N kick phases (circular fraction of beat against the current grid, strength-weighted) and returns a circular median offset. A 3 s fill is a minority of the ring, so the median rides it out.
Offset is re-expressed when the grid shifts, so a phase move does not corrupt the ring. The ring resets on a gridEpoch change.

The analyzer reports nextBeatTime and beat phase as the grid plus the held offset, once the ring has enough support and the offset passes a hysteresis band. With no kick events the offset is 0, so output equals main.

Attempt 1 uses a pre-registered offset (ring 16, hysteresis 0.05 beat). Attempt 2 uses a longer ring. Beatless and bar-level evidence stay stretch work, using the ring's concentration (circular variance) as a presence signal.

contracts: analyzer.pushBatch(batch) also reads onsetBand, onsetTime and onsetStrength; FEATURE_MESSAGE_VERSION is unchanged
KickPhase.push(time, strength, gridPhase) and KickPhase.offset(): number (beats, 0 when unsupported)
BeatTracker getters are unchanged; only the analyzer's reported nextBeatTime and phase carry the offset
pros: BeatTracker's tested contract fields and S2, S4b and S7 specs stay untouched, so blocking cells are unlikely to move
It avoids the slide-off failure, because the offset is learned over the whole beat circle and never competes with the envelope's correction
It is small and cheap: a fixed ring, no extra search
The same ring supplies a presence signal for the stretch slices
cons: It does not fix the tracker's internal grid, so lastBeatTime and the nextBeat-based gate and dance-clip consumers disagree unless they all read the output offset
It diverges from the framing in the plan, which asked for BeatTracker to hold a phase hypothesis
A global offset cannot follow a tempo or groove change that moves the kick-to-grid relation mid-track
risks: The scorecard may measure beat error from BeatTracker.lastBeatTime rather than analyzer output; if so, the scorecard and trace tool must read the corrected value (needs checking)
The offset could be a true kick-to-tap lag unique to summer2000 and hurt tracks where kicks and beat coincide; hysteresis and support gates must stay off for those
The 31 ms kick-to-tap lead is a median, so the residual near 40 ms may be tight
uncovered_acs: AC5 'phase move keeps the kick-supported phase' is met only at the output layer, not inside BeatTracker; the synthetic spec must be written against the analyzer

options.summary: Hybrid of O2 and O3. One kick-event input path (O2's ordered, allocation-free queue), then two structurally different bounded attempts, both prototyped offline first. Attempt A is O2's in-tracker kick-phase model, with a veto, hysteresis and a fill hold. Attempt B, only if A misses, is O3's output-layer kick offset. Stretch slices reuse the kick-phase support.
approach: S0 records post-merge main (after the D11 PRs) as the baseline, plus the kick-to-tap lead measured across every tapped track, not only summer2000

S1 adds the input path with no behavior change: rhythmTracker forwards the batch onsets, the analyzer's KickQueue releases band-0 events in time order before the first frame at or after them, and BeatTracker.pushKick records them. The offline replay (scorecard, trace:beats) uses the same path. Identity spec

S2 prototypes A and B in trace:beats with --set on summer2000 and the weak tracks, against pre-registered grids, and commits an it.fails synthetic (disagreeing envelope plus a fill) shown failing on main
S3 ships attempt A (O2) if it meets AC1 and AC2; otherwise it is recorded
S4 ships attempt B (O3) only if A missed. If both miss, summer2000 is accepted at its measured value (D4)
S5 closes the required cells with live runs; S6 beat presence and S7 bar-level read the kick-phase support

C2 kick input path
C3 tracker constants

pros: The input path ships alone and is identity-tested, so the risky part is isolated
Two structurally different attempts suit D4 better than two tunings of one idea
An offline prototype before app code avoids D11's premise failure
The lead constant is measured across all tapped tracks, which limits overfitting

decision_rationale: O4 is the top scorer. D11 failed because its premise was not checked before app code, so O4 prototypes offline first and isolates the new input path in its own identity-tested slice. O1 resembles D11's kick-preferring correction, which reached only 149.5 ms. O2 is the strongest single attempt, and O3 is a structurally different fallback that suits D4's two attempts. O3 alone drifts from BeatTracker's own grid.

design.overview: Baseline, input path, model behind off-by-default constants, offline go/no-go, then up to two enabling slices, then close, then stretch. S0 runs after the D11 PRs merge. It re-runs scorecard, sweep:gate, bench, size and the live cells, and rewrites the baseline in its own commit. It measures the kick-to-beat lead on the delivered stream, separately for the tapped and the synthetic tracks, and checks whether beatless and 6-8-time carry kick events at all, which decides S6 and S7. S1 adds the input path with no behavior change. analyzer.pushKicks(batch) is called once per batch, before that batch's frames, by rhythmTracker.onMessage and by every offline runner (scorecard replay.ts, beatTraceRunner, ablateRunner, setDirector, bench-tracker), so live and offline share one entry. Worklet events lag their frames (2-frame lookahead, 2-frame batches), so each event is delivered in arrival order with its own timestamp, which is at or before the latest frame time. A preallocated KickQueue holds band-0 events and clears on hardReset, a hard boundary and a time-base restart. S1 commits golden digests from post-merge main, and the bench gains BandOnsets with kick events. S2 commits KickPhaseModel and attempt B with every constant defaulting off, plus the trace columns and the specs, so what S2 measures is what ships. Attempt A: a decayed, strength-weighted kick histogram over the beat period. It is off while support is below KICK_SUPPORT_FLOOR. It vetoes envelope corrections that move the grid away from strong kick support. A kick-driven move bypasses the PHASE_MIN_BEATS and PHASE_SHIFT_BEATS streak gate, which D11 showed the rival never passes, and uses its own gate: margin above KICK_VETO_MARGIN for KICK_MOVE_BEATS consecutive beats. The per-beat correction freezes during a fill, defined as the coefficient of variation of the kick intervals over the last KICK_FILL_BEATS beats above KICK_FILL_CV while the envelope stays strong. It releases after KICK_RELEASE_BEATS with no support, or when kicks disagree with a sustained envelope phase for KICK_RECOVER_BEATS. The lead constant is applied only if the tapped and synthetic leads agree within 10 ms; otherwise there is no constant, and the hysteresis absorbs the lead. Attempt B offsets the analyzer's anchorTime inside updatePhase, so beatPhase, nextBeatTime, beatCount and barPhase move together, and measureBeat and the meter read the shifted anchor, keeping bar evidence on the visible beat. S2's go/no-go for S3: offline summer2000 at most 40 ms with AC2 green, the first kick-driven move at or before about 12 s or the hold covering the 12-14.8 s fill, and the grid within 40 ms of the taps before 18 s. S3 enables A, and S4 enables B only if A missed. If both miss, summer2000 is accepted at its measured value (D4). No phase move bumps gridEpoch (D7).

contracts.name: tracker.state beat contract
contracts.definition: beatPhase, nextBeatTime, beatCount, barPhase, lastBeatTime, periodSeconds, gridEpoch, phaseShiftCount and gridHitShare keep post-merge meaning. A phase move never bumps gridEpoch and increments phaseShiftCount; beatCount never decreases. Under attempt B, the offset is applied to the analyzer's anchorTime in updatePhase, so beatPhase, nextBeatTime, beatCount and barPhase move together, and measureBeat and the meter read the shifted anchor. The derived beat (nextBeatTime - time)/(1 - phase) in the replay equals the declared beat, by spec.

contracts.name: Kick input path
contracts.definition: analyzer.pushKicks(band, time, strength, count) is called once per FeatureBatch, before its frames, by rhythmTracker.onMessage and by every offline runner (scripts/scorecard/engine/replay.ts, scripts/rhythm-tools/beatTraceRunner.ts, ablateRunner.ts, setDirector.ts, scripts/bench-tracker.ts). FeatureBatch and FEATURE_MESSAGE_VERSION are unchanged. Band-0 events go into a preallocated KickQueue (capacity at least the worklet's per-batch onset capacity, oldest dropped on overflow, counted). They are delivered once each, in arrival order, with their own timestamp (at or before the latest frame time), to BeatTracker.pushKick(time: number, strength: number): void. The queue and model clear on hardReset, a hard boundary and a time-base restart. With the model off, output equals the golden digests.

contracts.name: Tracker constants
contracts.definition: Named exports in rhythmConfig.ts, all defaulting off until S3 or S4 enables them: KICK_QUEUE_CAPACITY, KICK_LEAD_SECONDS (0 unless S0's tapped and synthetic leads agree within 10 ms), KICK_PHASE_BINS, KICK_PHASE_DECAY, KICK_SUPPORT_FLOOR, KICK_VETO_MARGIN, KICK_MOVE_BEATS, KICK_FILL_BEATS, KICK_FILL_CV, KICK_RELEASE_BEATS, KICK_RECOVER_BEATS, KICK_OFFSET_RING, KICK_OFFSET_HYSTERESIS. All are overridable with ablate:rhythm --set and trace:beats --set. No runtime flag ships.

contracts.name: Kick-phase getters
contracts.definition: Read-only BeatTracker getters kickSupport (peak share, 0 to 1) and kickMargin (support at the best phase minus support at the grid phase), 0 with no kicks. Used by the trace tool and the stretch slices; not in tracker.state.

design.data: No persisted app data. The tapped .beats.json stay read-only. The baseline is rewritten by S0, then by each slice that improves cells, in its own commit after AC2 passes.
design.ux: No UI change. On summer2000 the visuals' beat should sit on the kicks within a few beats of enough kick evidence and stay there through the fill. Elsewhere nothing should change.
design.security_privacy: No change: client-side only. The audio stays local and is never committed.
design.observability: trace:beats prints kick support, margin, veto, hold and the KickQueue overflow count per beat. The scorecard cells and the existing debug:viz telemetry (gridEpoch, phaseShiftCount) cover the rest.
design.rollout: One PR per slice. S0, S2 and S5 are docs or test titles when nothing ships; S1 is refactor(rhythm); S3, S4, S6 and S7 are fix(rhythm). Each tracker PR runs scorecard, scorecard:check, sweep:gate, bench:tracker and size, lists every changed cell, and gets checked on the Cloudflare preview and with npm run dev. Any size-limit raise (at most 341.5 kB) goes in the PR that needs it, with the reason. If a D11 PR changes before merging, S0 is re-run first. Rollback is a PR revert.

test_strategy.unit: kickQueue.test.ts: arrival-order, exactly-once delivery with the worklet's lagging batch shape, overflow drop and count, clear on reset, no allocation after construction. A parity spec: the same batches through RhythmTracker.onMessage and the replay loop give identical pushKick calls. Golden digests from post-merge main with kicks fed and the model off. beatTracker.test.ts: disagreeing envelope plus fill keeps the kick phase under A; steady-but-wrong kicks and a tempo ramp recover within KICK_RECOVER_BEATS; support below the floor equals model off; resets; gridEpoch kept and phaseShiftCount bumped on moves; beatCount monotonic under B's offset; the replay's derived beat equals the declared one under B; the S2, S4b and S7 specs unchanged. Coverage stays at 95 percent or more.
test_strategy.integration: Offline: npm run scorecard, scorecard:check (exit 0, no hash change), sweep:gate, eval:rhythm --alignment, and trace:beats with kick events on summer2000, low-bpm-rnb and the weak tracks. Pre-registered grids, with all results in the PR.
test_strategy.e2e: npm run test:e2e after build: every visualizer renders, no console errors, contexts released.
test_strategy.manual: npm run dev and debug:viz on summer2000 with the dancer and cubes. scorecard:live for the dancer from the main checkout, one run at a time on an idle machine, repeating outliers.
test_strategy.non_functional: npm run size at most 341.5 kB total JS. bench:tracker median ratio at most 1.25 against post-merge main, interleaved. All new state is preallocated typed arrays.

risks.mitigation: The lead constant is applied only if the tapped and synthetic leads agree. Grids are fixed before running (S2). The synthetic and weak tracks must be no worse (AC2). The whole grid goes in the PR.

risks.description: Kicks sit off the beat on syncopated tracks, and the veto holds a wrong phase
risks.mitigation: Kick-driven moves need a sustained margin; the release rule; syncopation-no-kick and syncopationbass are in AC2; an off-beat kick spec.

risks.description: Even with lead compensation, the kick timing spread keeps summer2000 above 40 ms
risks.mitigation: S2 measures both attempts offline before app code. D4 caps it at two attempts, then accepts the measured value.

risks.description: The offline replay and the live path deliver kicks differently
risks.mitigation: One pushKicks entry is called by onMessage and all five runners. A parity spec with the worklet's lagging batch shape. S5's live runs.
Fixed rings and O(bins) work per beat; size and bench in every PR; the raise is at most 3 kB.

risks.description: A D11 PR changes or is dropped before merging, which invalidates the baseline
risks.mitigation: S0 runs only after the merges and is re-run if any of them changes.

risks.description: The veto or hold freezes a wrong grid on music the scorecard lacks (kicks steady while the groove shifts, ramps, mislabeled bass kicks)
risks.mitigation: Disagreement release after KICK_RECOVER_BEATS, the support floor, and the AC5 steady-but-wrong and ramp synthetics.

open_questions.question: Are worklet onsetTime (window centre) and frame times on the same clock with a fixed offset? Settled by S1's ordering spec
Should a kick-driven phase move be slewed over a beat or two, to soften the known abrupt re-align?
open_questions.owner: implementer of S3, confirmed by Trevor

open_questions.question: If both attempts miss, does summer2000 need a full multi-hypothesis particle-style tracker plan, or is acceptance final?

findings.finding: C2, AC3 and S1 get the ordering direction wrong. They guard against a batch's events that 'lead its frames' and release each kick 'before the first frame at or after its time'. In the worklet the events lag. BandOnsets decides a candidate frame ONSET_LOOKAHEAD_FRAMES (2) later (bandOnsets.ts:278, 299, 305), and BATCH_FRAMES is 2, so an event's time is usually older than its own batch's first frame. rhythmProcessor.worklet.test.ts:318-341 asserts this and requires crossings > 0. By the time pushBatch sees a kick, frames later than it have already been analysed. The plan's release rule cannot be met, and a spec built on 'leading' events would pass while the real shape goes untested. The kick also reaches the model about 25 to 45 ms after its timestamp. That delay changes what KICK_LEAD_SECONDS and the 'hold' timing mean.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite C2 and AC3 as: each event is delivered exactly once, in arrival order, with its own timestamp, before the first frame of the batch that carried it. The model must accept event time less than or equal to the latest frame time. Make the S1 ordering spec use the worklet's crossing batch shape (the existing test fixture). Measure the lead constant on the delivered stream, not on raw event times.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan. C2 and AC3 now say events lag: delivered once, in arrival order, with their own timestamp, before the first frame of the batch that carried them. The spec uses the worklet's lagging fixture, and the lead is measured on the delivered stream (S0).

findings.finding: C2 says the offline replay 'uses the same call' as the live path (pushBatch), and K4 relies on that. It does not. The scorecard's deliver() (scripts/scorecard/engine/replay.ts:303-326) calls analyzer.pushFrame per frame, with updatePhase between frames, and hands the batch to the hub only afterwards. beatTraceRunner.ts:51-74, ablateRunner.ts:16-37, setDirector.ts:129-182 and scripts/bench-tracker.ts do the same. A drain placed in pushBatch is never exercised by the scorecard, trace:beats or ablate, so the offline wins that decide S3 and S4 would use different delivery code from the live app. S1's draft_paths cover only scripts/scorecard/ and omit scripts/rhythm-tools/ and bench-tracker.ts.
findings.suggestion: Give live and every runner one entry point, for example analyzer.pushKicks(batch) called before the batch's frames. Alternatively, drain inside pushFrame against a queue the runners fill. List all five runners in S1's draft_paths. Add a spec that feeds the same batch sequence through RhythmTracker.onMessage and through the replay loop and asserts identical pushKick calls.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan. One analyzer.pushKicks entry is called by onMessage and all five runners, listed in S1's draft_paths, with a parity spec (AC3).

findings.finding: Attempt B and C1 are inconsistent with what consumers read. C1 says B puts the offset on 'nextBeatTime and beatCount' and that the hub, gate and dancer 'read only tracker.state'. They read beatPhase and beatCount (replay.ts:260-275, computeDanceTiming), and the scorecard and eval/detect.ts:85 derive the beat time from beatPhase plus nextBeatTime ((nextBeatTime - time)/(1 - phase), replay.ts:318). Shifting nextBeatTime without beatPhase corrupts the derived period and the measured error. Shifting beatCount alone moves nothing visible. The offset D11 measured is large: kicks sit 0.25 to 0.375 beat, about 120 to 175 ms, from the grid. BeatTracker, measureBeat(lastBeatTime), meter, downbeat bookkeeping, gridHitShare and the boundary tempo cue would all stay on the unshifted grid. That puts accent and bar evidence about 0.3 beat from the beat the user sees. AC2 lists no barPhase or meter cell. Moving the offset in an output layer is also a different thing from 'a phase hold' and is easy to game on the one cell.
findings.suggestion: Define B concretely as an offset on anchorTime inside updatePhase, so beatPhase, nextBeatTime, beatCount and barPhase all move together. Say whether measureBeat and the meter read the shifted anchor. Add specs that beatCount stays monotonic when the offset changes and that the replay's derived beat equals the declared one. Add the meter and downbeat cells and the dance-clip cells to AC2 for S4. Settle this in S2, as C1 promises, before B is attempted.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan. B offsets anchorTime in updatePhase, so beatPhase, nextBeatTime, beatCount and barPhase move together, and measureBeat and the meter read the shifted anchor (C1). There are specs for monotonic beatCount and the derived beat equalling the declared one, and AC2 adds the meter, downbeat and dance-clip cells for S4.

findings.finding: AC4 (bench ratio at most 1.25) cannot measure the new cost. scripts/bench-tracker.ts and benchTracker.ts feed only OnsetExtractor/packFrame frames. They run no BandOnsets and send no kick events, so KickQueue and KickPhaseModel never run, and the ratio against main stays near 1.0 whatever the model costs. Per-beat histogram work lands on the live main thread next to the visualizer. AC3's 'identical to post-merge main' is also not a repository-checkable statement: a unit spec has no main to compare against.
findings.suggestion: Extend the bench to run BandOnsets and pass events (base ref without pushKick runs kickless as it does today). Report both the kickless ratio and the with-kicks ratio. For AC3, commit golden outputs (or a pinned digest of the state sequence) from post-merge main on a few synthetic tracks, and also assert that kick events with the model switched off give the same output.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan. The bench runs BandOnsets and feeds kicks, and reports kickless and with-kicks ratios (AC4, S1). AC3 now checks committed golden digests from post-merge main.

findings.finding: S2 is circular and its contracts are not frozen before use. S2 must run A and B and print 'support, margin, veto and hold' (C4), but kickPhase.ts and the beatTracker.ts changes are not in S2's draft_paths. They arrive in S3 and S4. C3 (the KICK_* constants) and C4 (the getters) are attached to S1 and S2 although their code ships later. The likely outcome repeats D11. The prototype is scratch, uncommitted code, the S2 record says 'A works at constants X', and S3 re-implements it. The reimplementation then differs, and the pre-registered grid no longer describes what shipped. S2 is also marked R0 while it commits an it.fails spec and changes trace tooling.
findings.suggestion: Have S2 commit the model and attempt-B offset behind default-off constants (C3 already requires that defaults reproduce main). S3 and S4 then become constant changes plus guard enabling, and what is measured is what ships. Attach C3 and C4 to S2. Add a go/no-go to S2: no S3 unless the offline summer2000 result is at most 40 ms with AC2 green.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan. S2 commits the model and B behind off-by-default constants with C3 and C4, at R1, with a go/no-go. S3 and S4 only enable constants, so what is measured is what ships.

findings.finding: KICK_LEAD_SECONDS is taken from kick-to-tap offsets on 'every tapped track' (S0, O4, K1). A tap lead includes the tapper's latency, and the .beats.json files are human taps. D11 S1 shows taps jittering up to 50 ms and kick-to-tap quartiles of -73 and +9 ms around the 31 ms median. The synthetic tracks have exact sidecar beats with kicks on the beat, and alignment.test.ts holds them to a median error of 20 ms or better. A constant compensation applied wherever the kick model acts shifts those by about 31 ms. AC2 names only passing cells with a tolerance and no synthetic-alignment guard. An error floor of about 31 ms against a 40 ms target also leaves very little room.
findings.suggestion: In S0, report the lead separately for tapped and for synthetic tracks. Apply compensation only if the two agree. Otherwise drop the constant and judge the kick phase relative to the grid with the hysteresis band absorbing it. Add the synthetic alignment cells (beat error, first lock) to AC2 explicitly.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan. S0 measures the lead separately for tapped and synthetic tracks, the constant is applied only if they agree within 10 ms (C3), and AC2 guards the synthetic alignment cells.

findings.finding: Attempt A's kick-driven move re-uses the evidence class D11 measured as a miss: kick events as a phase histogram (153 ms) and a half-beat flip (176 to 199 ms). The plan's non-goals forbid retrying 'kick-weighted phase bins'. What is new is the veto and the fill hold, which is a fair reading of the 'slides off within 2 s' result. Three gaps remain. It is not stated whether the kick-driven move uses the existing phaseBeats streak gate (PHASE_MIN_BEATS and PHASE_SHIFT_BEATS), which D11 found the rival never passes, or bypasses it. There is no timeline: lock is at 8.0 s, kicks are regular before the fill only partly (42 of 58 taps have one within 150 ms), the fill is 12 to 14.8 s, and the latest first move that still allows AC1 is about 18 s. A hysteresis of N beats on a decayed histogram may only fire after the fill ends. The fill hold is defined as 'envelope strong, kicks irregular', with no measure of irregular.
findings.suggestion: State that the kick-driven move bypasses the streak gate, and name the replacement gate. In S2's pre-registration, record the time of the first kick-driven move and the time the grid first lands within 40 ms of the taps. Make 'first move at or before about 12 s, or the hold covers the fill' an S2 go/no-go. Define 'irregular' numerically.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan. The kick-driven move bypasses the phase streak gate and uses KICK_VETO_MARGIN for KICK_MOVE_BEATS. A fill is defined numerically (KICK_FILL_CV over KICK_FILL_BEATS). S2 records the first move time and the first time within 40 ms, with a go/no-go of a move by about 12 s or a hold covering the fill.

findings.finding: The veto and hold can freeze a wrong grid in cases the scorecard does not contain: a real phase change that the kicks do not follow (a drum loop that stays steady while the groove shifts), a ramp, and live sources with sparse or mislabeled kicks (bass notes classified as kick, which the plan already lists under bassline-kick-120). The release rule (M beats with no kick support) fires only when kicks vanish, not when they stay but disagree. The tests list 'off-beat kicks release after KICK_RELEASE_BEATS', but no case has kicks present, steady and wrong.
findings.suggestion: Add one synthetic: kicks stay on the old phase while the rest of the groove moves by a quarter beat (and a tempo ramp). Pin a bounded recovery time (for example, the grid follows within K beats). Include it in AC5. Turn the model off when kick support stays below a floor, so sparse-kick tracks such as low-bpm-rnb (13 of 35 taps have a kick) provably behave as on main.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan. Disagreement release (KICK_RECOVER_BEATS), the support floor, and steady-but-wrong and ramp synthetics are in AC5 and K7.

findings.finding: Stretch slices S6 and S7 (beat presence, bar level) rest on an unchecked assumption that kick support separates beatless and 6-8-time. D11's S6 note says beatless has a real 140 bpm periodicity that no presence signal told apart from a beat. A track whose kicks are periodic will also show high kick support on the proposed period. S7 is sized L, and S8 found the missing evidence is the bar itself (6 eighths), which a kick-onset pattern may not carry on 6-8-time. Both depend on S5, which depends on S4, a conditional slice.
findings.suggestion: Before S6 and S7, add a one-hour offline check in S0 or S2 on whether beatless and 6-8-time have kick events and what their support and pattern look like; cancel the stretch slice if not. Reword S5's depends_on to 'S3, and S4 when it ran'.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan. S0 checks the kick events on beatless and 6-8-time and cancels S6 or S7 if they carry no usable evidence. S4 is recorded as not needed when A shipped, so S5's dependency always completes.

findings.finding: AC2 requires every gate.secondsAfterLock cell on a passing track not to rise by more than 0.5 s, while D6 and the non-goals say gate seconds are reported and not tuned. summer2000, half-time-shuffle and lonley are already failing, so the check is hard to read on the tracks most likely to move. 'no .beats.json hash changed' holds trivially. K4 and C2 also never say what happens to queued kicks on analyzer reset, hardReset, song change, or worklet restart after skipped blocks (the worklet restarts the time base and resets BandOnsets), so stale kick times could survive a reset.
findings.suggestion: Scope the gate-seconds check to cells that pass on post-merge main and say failing tracks are reported only. Add a spec that KickQueue and the kick model clear on hardReset, a hard boundary and a time-base restart.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan. Gate-seconds checks are scoped to cells passing on post-merge main, failing ones are reported only, the trivial hash clause is dropped, and reset clearing is in C2 and AC3.

freeze_first.name: tracker.state beat contract
freeze_first.definition: beatPhase, nextBeatTime, beatCount, barPhase, lastBeatTime, periodSeconds, gridEpoch, phaseShiftCount and gridHitShare keep post-merge meaning. A phase move never bumps gridEpoch and increments phaseShiftCount; beatCount never decreases. Under attempt B, the offset is applied to the analyzer's anchorTime in updatePhase, so beatPhase, nextBeatTime, beatCount and barPhase move together, and measureBeat and the meter read the shifted anchor. The derived beat (nextBeatTime - time)/(1 - phase) in the replay equals the declared beat, by spec.

freeze_first.name: Kick input path
freeze_first.definition: analyzer.pushKicks(band, time, strength, count) is called once per FeatureBatch, before its frames, by rhythmTracker.onMessage and by every offline runner (scripts/scorecard/engine/replay.ts, scripts/rhythm-tools/beatTraceRunner.ts, ablateRunner.ts, setDirector.ts, scripts/bench-tracker.ts). FeatureBatch and FEATURE_MESSAGE_VERSION are unchanged. Band-0 events go into a preallocated KickQueue (capacity at least the worklet's per-batch onset capacity, oldest dropped on overflow, counted). They are delivered once each, in arrival order, with their own timestamp (at or before the latest frame time), to BeatTracker.pushKick(time: number, strength: number): void. The queue and model clear on hardReset, a hard boundary and a time-base restart. With the model off, output equals the golden digests.

freeze_first.name: Tracker constants
freeze_first.definition: Named exports in rhythmConfig.ts, all defaulting off until S3 or S4 enables them: KICK_QUEUE_CAPACITY, KICK_LEAD_SECONDS (0 unless S0's tapped and synthetic leads agree within 10 ms), KICK_PHASE_BINS, KICK_PHASE_DECAY, KICK_SUPPORT_FLOOR, KICK_VETO_MARGIN, KICK_MOVE_BEATS, KICK_FILL_BEATS, KICK_FILL_CV, KICK_RELEASE_BEATS, KICK_RECOVER_BEATS, KICK_OFFSET_RING, KICK_OFFSET_HYSTERESIS. All are overridable with ablate:rhythm --set and trace:beats --set. No runtime flag ships.

freeze_first.name: Kick-phase getters
freeze_first.definition: Read-only BeatTracker getters kickSupport (peak share, 0 to 1) and kickMargin (support at the best phase minus support at the grid phase), 0 with no kicks. Used by the trace tool and the stretch slices; not in tracker.state.
